BdpScope.description: The URL of a BDP scope (a store).

Scope.description: The decoder ring for every id — the namespace an `id` resolves in, and so how to read the `id`. The one place the three readings are defined; everything that carries an id is read through this.

Rev.description: A resource-version token — opaque by definition; compared for exact equality only, never inspected.

Digest.description: A content-addressed rev (sha256 / commit) — a Rev that is a digest.

ResourceId.description: The identity of a resource — a scope, an id within it, and an optional revision. The wire URL is the projection (scope URL ⊕ id).

ResourceRef.description: A reference to a resource is just its id.

ref.description: A typed (phantom) reference — the by-reference form. `T` is the referenced resource's BODY type; it is checker-only and erases on the wire (a `ref` is a `ResourceId`).

pinned.description: A reference pinned to one exact revision (`rev` present).

unpinned.description: An unpinned reference (`rev` absent) — floats to the current revision.

rep.description: The representation of a versioned resource — the protocol envelope around a typed `body: T`. The by-value form a read returns; `ref<T>` is the by-reference form. `Resource` is `rep<any>`, an untyped representation.

Resource.description: An untyped representation — `rep<any>`. Used where the body type is unknown or open (a mixed listing, a generic read).

Bead.description: A vacuous kind marker — a body type tagged `is Bead` is a package-authored record. It adds no members; it marks intention, lets a signature demand a bead (`ref<Bead>`), and carries the enforcement that a bead body is a record under a package authority. It is the implicit ROOT of a bead's kind path and contributes NO path segment: `type Issue is Bead` ⇒ kind `"issue"`.

Content.description: A vacuous kind marker — a body type tagged `is Content` is a registry-named (media-type) resource with an opaque body (bytes / text). The complement of `Bead`; a root marker, no path segment.

PathString.description: A slash-delimited path — `"issue/task"` (a bead kind) or `"text/plain"` (a content media type).

Authority.description: The resource that names a `type` — a package (for a bead) or a registry like IANA (for content). A ResourceRef, so the pin lives in its `rev`.

PackageRef.description: A pinned reference to a Package resource — an Authority that is a package (a bead's authority).

Metadata.description: Opaque, open per-resource (or per-call) sidecar — data the protocol does not interpret.

Provenance.description: Who took part in the change that made a revision, how the Resource's present period began, and when. `previousRevision` is the before-image pointer — the basis for compensation — and rides in the post-image, so a ChangeEvent carries it for free.

Principal.description: An identity that took part in a change — a person, agent or service account. A role grants no permission; authorization is a separate decision.

IdentityBasis.description: How a service established a principal's identity.

StorageClass.description: How a Resource is kept — whether it is persisted, not whether it is versioned (that is the scope's revision model). Durable is replicated and exported; ephemeral is local and never exported; intrinsic is computed by the service, not stored (capability beads are intrinsic).

AbsoluteUri.description: Any absolute URI — a Problem `type`, a Principal `id`; need not resolve. NOT a resource reference (those are `ref<T>`).

SemVer.description: A semantic-version string (a package's declared version).

integer.description: A whole number — JSON `number` restricted to an integer value. Distinct from `number` (which admits fractions) so a typed or generated client maps it to an integer type (e.g. i64); on the wire it is an integer-valued JSON number. Use `integer` for counts, bounds, positions and priorities; keep `number` for genuinely fractional values (a score, a ratio).

rel.description: The relationship construct and its declaration form. `rel<F, T>` is a `Bead` body type that carries `source` (type F, the owning endpoint that asserts the relationship) and `target` (type T), plus the relationship type's own properties; its resource is `rep<rel<F, T>>`. A relationship type is declared `type X is <modifiers> rel<F, T> { <edge-fields> }` — a nominal refinement whose trailing record extends the body; a bare `<modifiers> rel<F, T>` is the same shape without the nominal identity. The declared name is the body type; `ref<X>` references the relationship, `rep<X>` is its representation.

Alias.description: A named pointer — a second name for a resource. The alias's own id is the name, under the reserved `sys/aliases/` root; its `target` names the resource the name stands for.

TypeDef.description: A type-definition bead body — one node in the single-`is` refinement tree. Its resource is `rep<TypeDef>`.

PropertyDeclaration.description: One property in a type's body — its name, its type, and its access mode. `computed` marks a derived, revision-transparent property (see §1.8); `serviceManaged` is the sibling write-access mode. Property optionality rides the property's `type`.

ParameterDeclaration.description: One parameter of an operation — its name, its type, and whether it is required. A default value is NOT a core concern; it is a CLI surface hint carried outside the protocol.

BeadSchema.description: A type written down as a value — the ref-preserving type representation. (A `schema` has no identity, so a type-as-value is a `schema`.)

LocalName.description: A short identifier token for a view or a well-known name; leading letter.

PackageElementRef.description: A bundled reference to a package element — a package authority plus the element's relative path.

ElementPath.description: A package-relative element path (the single-`is` chain).

TypeRef.description: A reference to a type element.

OperationRef.description: A reference to an operation element.

ChannelRef.description: A reference to a channel element.

Channel.description: A channel-descriptor bead body — its two event schemas, direction, and delivery characteristics. Its resource is `rep<Channel>`.

Retention.description: How far back a cursor can resume; below the floor a cursor faults `cursor-expired` and the reader resyncs (list-bootstrap + follow from head).

Ordinal.description: An event's position in its stream; monotone within one Channel.

Cursor.description: Opaque, transport-independent resume token, bound to one stream and the selection it came from; refused elsewhere. Also the point an export is cut at.

Transport.description: The transport encoding a caller selects (the `--format` arm): `page` (windowed JSON pages), `jsonl` (bulk JSON-lines), or `sse` (live SSE). The token mirrors the typed projection — `page<T>` / `jsonl<T>` / `sse<T>`. `page` is the windowed encoding; `jsonl` is the bulk encoding, offered by the bulk reads (`export`, `pull`, stdlib `query`) but NOT the windowed resource reads `list`/`revisions` (which are `page`-only); `sse` is valid only on a `source` (a live feed, `pull`), and a `snapshot` (list/query/revisions/export) does not carry it in its support set.

ReadRequest.description: The input to a streaming read — where to resume, how much, the transport, and per-item shaping. ONE request type for every read, `source` ([[core.lumen#pull]]) and `snapshot` ([[core.lumen#list]] / [[core.lumen#revisions]] / [[core.lumen#export]] / stdlib `query`) alike; the valid `format` set is DERIVED from the read's nature (a `source` admits `sse`, a `snapshot` does not). `after` (a cursor) xor `from` (a fresh ordinal) are mutually exclusive. The target is the op's first parameter, not restated here.

Page.description: One finite page of a stream — the windowed floor every service offers: one request, one page, nothing held open.

PushEvent.description: One event offered to [[core.lumen#push]]. `body` is the payload (the channel's `pushSchema` type — which MAY be any value, not only a record, so `body: T` is deliberately unconstrained); `ordinal`, when present, is the pusher-assigned position that makes the append idempotent (keyed). Absent, the channel assigns the ordinal.

PushAck.description: What [[core.lumen#push]] returns — the high-water ordinal accepted, a per-event result, and the backpressure signal (`credit` + optional `retryAfter`). A short `results` with `credit: 0` and a deferred tail is normal flow, not an error.

PushResult.description: The fate of one offered event.

Operation.description: An operation-descriptor bead body — the call contract, the implementation, and the behavioural guarantees. Its resource is `rep<Operation>`.

Signature.description: An operation's call contract — its interface, kept separate from the implementation and the effect markers.

Cause.description: A correlation token shared down a causal chain — minted at an initiating (often detached) call and propagated unchanged to every call it sets off; `causedBy` points at the parent cause. Correlates all of one initiation's work. See bdp.md §6.

CallId.description: A correlation token naming one call — a node in the call tree; `calledBy` points at the parent call. Distinct from `Cause` (correlation to an initiation) and `Transaction` (the atomic commit). Diagnostic-tier.

Transaction.description: A correlation token naming one atomic commit — shared by every change that commits together. Propagated by enlistment, not unconditionally (Required / RequiresNew / detach); crossing a scope forces a new one. See bdp.md §6.

IdempotencyKey.description: Caller-chosen key that makes a retried write safe to collapse onto the first effect.

Request.description: What a caller sends to `call`. `arguments` is a name/value list whose shape the Operation's `parameters` dictate.

Reply.description: What a `call` returns — flat, no context wrapper. `outcome` keeps the domain `Result` nested in `Outcome`.

Result.description: A callable's own verdict — succeeded with a value, or failed with its declared error.

Outcome.description: What happened to an invocation — the domain Result, or a non-domain fate.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document — what a `fault` carries, and the body of a failing response from the data primitives.

AsyncResult.description: The async result of one `call` — a handle you show for the record and `cancel` to kill. References a one-and-done source Channel that fires the Reply on settlement.

PackageDef.description: A package bead body — its declared version and its elements. Its resource is `rep<PackageDef>`.

IdRoot.description: A prefix-rooted auto-id proposal (the server mints the leaf).

selector.description: A read projection over a representation — include/omit subtrees (JSON Pointer) and expand. Query-string, so a projected read has its own cacheable identity; `type`/`id` are never dropped.

JsonPointer.description: A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into a representation.

JsonPatchOp.description: One RFC 6902 operation. In `patch`, paths are root-addressed over the rep (`/body`, `/metadata`, `/type`, `/authority`; the rest is read-only).

JsonPatch.description: An ordered list of JSON Patch operations — the `patch` body, and a change-event patch payload.

Envelope.description: The query-tier body-form envelope — the ONE place a write guard rides a body. Used only when an over-budget `precondition` (or representation) spills to `POST /{id}/-/{put|patch|delete}`; the direct `put`/`patch`/`delete` verbs never carry it. Media type `application/vnd.bdp.envelope+json`.

Filter.description: The low-bar list filter — a flat conjunction (and) of simple field conditions, exactly the query-string-expressible set. The baseline every service supports; the full boolean/traversal predicate is a stdlib capability (`query`, [[stdlib.lumen#query]]), not base.

listCondition.description: One flat field condition. `isType` matches against the type-path (`type.id`): `prefix` ⊑ (the "is it an issue(-ish)?" test), `exact` =.

FieldPath.description: A field path as a segment array (disambiguates dotted keys); selector/patch keep JSON Pointer.

RelativeId.description: A type-path as a local id segment, relative to the scope (the target for isType's prefix/exact match).

ChangeEvent.description: Core's report of one committed change to one Resource — Created / Updated / Deleted — or an operation-frame boundary (CallEnter / CallLeave) for an unsafe call. A top-level DU on lifecycle (a relationship change is an Updated to the relationship resource). `subject.rev` is the new (or tombstone) revision. Provenance rides in the post-image where there is one and is explicit where there is not.

ChangeEnvelope.description: Fields common to EVERY arm — position, time, and the correlation tokens. No subject: a resource arm adds that via [[core.lumen#ResourceChange]]; a frame arm (CallEnter / CallLeave) has none.

ResourceChange.description: What the resource arms (Created / Updated / Deleted) add to [[core.lumen#ChangeEnvelope]] — the subject and its denormalized type. A frame arm carries none of these.

Created.description: A resource admitted. Full post-image; its provenance is the representation's provenance.

Updated.description: A resource changed. `content` is the orthogonal encoding axis — `full` carries a post-image (provenance rides in it), `patch` is a delta with explicit provenance.

Deleted.description: A resource retired — the tombstone. No post-image, so provenance is explicit; `subject.rev` is the tombstone revision.

CallEnter.description: An operation frame opened — the open boundary of an unsafe call on the changefeed. Carries the operation; its callId / cause / transaction ride the envelope.

CallLeave.description: An operation frame closed — the close boundary of an unsafe call. Carries the outcome (success / failure / fault / canceled, with the value); its callId / cause / transaction ride the envelope.

ChangeContent.description: The change payload for Updated — full-vs-patch, the encoding axis (orthogonal to lifecycle).

ExportRecord.description: One line of an export. The export is a strict in-order serialization, so a record's POSITION in the stream is its ordinal — the resume key a resumable `import` acks against ([[core.lumen#import]]). No ordinal field is added to the record: its position carries it, anchored on import by the request's `fromOrdinal` when the stream is chunked across requests. `ExportBegin` carries the changefeed cut the export was taken at.

ExportBegin.description: The opening line — the Scope and the cursor the export was cut at (where a consumer resumes the changefeed). Told apart from a Resource line by `kind`.

ExportEnd.description: The closing line — a count of the Resource records, so a truncated file (one ending without this line) is detectable and never taken for whole.

ImportStrategy.description: How `import` merges — strategy and id remap.

ImportReport.description: The import tally — counts and any conflicted records. It is the `tallies` of the final [[core.lumen#ImportAck]] (the call that consumes `ExportEnd`); the old terminal whole-batch report folds here. Also returned directly by pack ops that summarize a bulk load.

ImportResult.description: The fate of one offered export record, in stream order — mirrors [[core.lumen#PushResult]] with an added hard-reject arm. The record is identified by its stream ordinal (its position in the export).

ImportAck.description: What [[core.lumen#import]] returns — the push-style acknowledgement for a resumable, backpressured bulk load, mirroring [[core.lumen#PushAck]]. `acceptedThrough` is the high-water record ordinal PROCESSED by this call; the importer re-offers the deferred tail from `acceptedThrough + 1`. The call that consumes `ExportEnd` sets `complete: true` and carries the final `tallies`; a one-shot (non-resumable) import returns a single ack already `complete`.

ImportId.description: A caller-minted token identifying one resumable import across its requests. Opaque to the scope; its only job is to correlate a resumed batch with the `acceptedThrough` the scope is tracking, and to keep concurrent imports into one scope from crossing.

ServiceDescriptor.description: The bounded discovery signpost returned by `GET /` (a scope's base URL) — a THIN envelope that names the protocol and LINKS to the rest, never embedding it. With `get` and `/sys/capabilities`, it is the mandatory floor.

ServiceLinks.description: The discovery link set — RFC 8631 web-service link relations to the service's other resources. A relation's absence means the service does not offer it. Mirrored in the `Link` header.

Capabilities.description: What a scope advertises through discovery — read it by `get` on the well-known `/sys/capabilities` resource. Its primitive capabilities are partitioned by package (`core` is the base; other packages advertise their own), à la carte: a primitive is supported iff its capability is present. Scope-wide traits that are not per-primitive live in `scope`.

CoreCapabilities.description: The `core` package's advertised primitives, à la carte — a primitive is supported iff its field is present, and its value carries that primitive's limits. `get` is always present (the floor). Each limit record is the advertise side of a dual: the matching `limit-exceeded` (422) is the enforce side. These are the core primitives that advertise in the core record; `call` and `cancel` (operations) advertise under their own packages, not here (§3.3).

ScopeCapabilities.description: A scope's scope-wide traits — the capabilities that are neither per-primitive nor pack-specific. Storage classes, the revision model, and whether aliases are supported live here.

AliasCaps.description: Advertised for `aliases` — its presence signals that `Alias` resources under `sys/aliases/` and the scope-root overlay are active. An alias is always single-hop and same-scope (no chains); any further limits (e.g. a cap on aliases per target) ride here.

RevisionModel.description: A scope's revision model — a scope-wide trait, stated outright (no implicit default).

IdModel.description: A scope's id model — a scope-wide trait, stated outright (no implicit default). Whether an id retired by `delete` is permanently spent or may be minted again.

ConditionKind.description: One operator in the low-bar `list` filter. The richer filter / query language is a corelib (query-pack) capability, not core.

PullCaps.description: Limits advertised for `pull` (the changefeed and declared streams).

PutCaps.description: Limits advertised for `put` — which write guards it honors. The `precondition` operator set is ⊆ [[core.lumen#ListCaps]] `conditions`.

PatchCaps.description: Limits advertised for `patch`. The `precondition` operator set is ⊆ [[core.lumen#ListCaps]] `conditions`.

DeleteCaps.description: Limits advertised for `delete`. The `precondition` operator set is ⊆ [[core.lumen#ListCaps]] `conditions`.

RevisionsCaps.description: Presence advertises that prior revisions are addressable (`revisions`); offered only by a `versioned` scope.
